name: GB200 NVL72
notes: Official NVIDIA Blackwell datasheet's Technical Specifications table (p.7) gives 'Total Fast Memory: Up to 30TB' (30,500 GB used here, matching the 'Up to 30.5TB' figure from the Key Features list on p.2) and 'Supports up to 13.5TB of HBM3E' (also p.2 Key Features; p.7 table gives per-GPU 186GB x 72 = 13,392GB, consistent with the vendor-rounded 13.5TB figure -- 13,500 GB used here as the vendor-stated headline number). total_fp32_tflops (5760) is derived (80 TFLOPS/GPU per p.7 table x 72 GPUs) since no rack-level total FP32 is independently vendor-published; no independent corroboration found yet for this GB200 total (unlike the analogous HGX B200 PCF cross-check) -- flagged as derived, not directly sourced. Per datasheet footnote 1, FP4/FP8/FP6 totals are sparse-spec only. FP8 and FP6 totals published as one combined figure. No total TF32, FP16/BF16, FP64, or INT8 rack-level figures vendor-published; left null. networking left null -- this datasheet does not name a specific NIC/fabric for GB200 NVL72 (mentions InfiniBand generically in performance-comparison footnotes only, not as a spec-table entry); needs a follow-up source (e.g. NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 product page or DGX GB200 datasheet) before populating. power_kw_max not stated in this datasheet; other NVIDIA/partner docs (Supermicro GB200 NVL72 datasheet) independently cite 125-135kW per rack -- left null here rather than treating an analog-document estimate as this record's sourced value.

_sources.total_cpu_memory_gb: https://www.primeline-solutions.com/media/categories/server/nach-gpu/nvidia-hgx-h200/nvidia-blackwell-b200-datasheet.pdf (p.2, Key Features: 'Up to 17 terabytes (TB) of LPDDR5X memory')
_sources.total_fast_memory_gb: https://www.primeline-solutions.com/media/categories/server/nach-gpu/nvidia-hgx-h200/nvidia-blackwell-b200-datasheet.pdf (p.2, Key Features: 'Up to 30.5TB of fast-access memory'; p.7 table rounds to 'Up to 30TB')
_sources.total_fp32_tflops: Derived: 80 TFLOPS/GPU (p.7 Technical Specifications table) x 72 GPUs. Not independently corroborated by a second source at time of writing.
